lines.text: [pulse color=#ffd28a freq=1.4]A year on from the abyss.[/pulse] Coffee is hotter than it used to be.

lines.speaker: Mentor
lines.text: You've seen the dragon up close. Do you want to kill it, ride it, or walk away?

choices.text: Change the system from inside. Director track.
Start my own thing. No more reporting.
Consulting. Teaching. Half time. Family time.

lines.text: Your child, now seventeen, slumps onto the sofa.

lines.speaker: Child
lines.text: Everyone says I should do engineering. But I want to do design.

choices.text: I followed the safe path. Don't repeat my mistakes.
Here is my full story. You decide.

lines.text: The dragon. Smaller now. Or you are larger. Or both.
You sit across from it like an old colleague at a farewell dinner.

choices.text: I built you. I can let you go.
You taught me. Now I leave.
I'll teach others to recognise you sooner.

lines.text: The last office goodbye. Or the first day of something new.
A child's wedding. A parent's anniversary. A book you finally read.
You opened a small school for kids who could not afford coaching.
Your old colleagues call sometimes. Some of them have quit.
[Ending: Legacy Builder]
The flat is smaller. The mornings are slower. Your spouse is reading on the same sofa.
Your child sends you a meme. You laugh out loud.
[Ending: Balanced Fulfillment]
The corner office. The car. The corporate award on the shelf.
You eat dinner alone more nights than not.
[Ending: Corporate Sovereign]
The doctor uses the word maintenance, not recovery.
You write a long letter to your younger self. You actually send it, to your kid.
[Ending: Tragic Regret]
You moved. New town. Slower internet. Better mangoes.
You started teaching local kids on Saturdays without quite meaning to.
[Ending: Simple Redemption]
